thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'prod-gpu-pool-3' queue length > 1200 (SLO breach risk). Autoscaler attempted to scale but hit max_replicas=60. Recent rollout 'lm-v4-hotwarmup' detected high context/KV warmup.

Alex W: seeing 5xx and 429s on generation endpoints, token latency spiking. Triage starting.

Sara K: confirmed. Metrics: p95 token latency 1.2s -> 4.5s, active requests queued 1200+, per-GPU mem pressure 98%. Autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts failing with "quota exceeded" from provider.

Alex W: logs (snippet):
```
2026-03-15T16:02:10Z ERROR autoscaler: scale attempt failed: RequestLimitExceeded
2026-03-15T16:02:11Z WARN serving: enqueue len=1234 model=lm-v4-hotwarmup ctx_len=4096 kv_warmup=true
2026-03-15T16:02:12Z ERROR runtime: OOM on allocation for kv-cache warmup shard
```

Jamie L: oncall handoff incoming in 10m. Quick note: rollout of lm-v4-hotwarmup started 16:00 UTC — rollback flag available.

Megan R: customer impact tracker - initial customers seeing errors: acme-inc (prod), quickchat (staging -> prod), searchly (prod). All flagged for 429s/timeouts. Estimated 15% of hosted traffic hitting fallback model.

TJ (oncall): immediate mitigations I can do: 1) pause/rollback rollout, 2) apply temporary rate-limiter on the route to shed permissive traffic, 3) increase autoscaler max_replicas if cloud quota allows. Which do we prefer?

Alex W: priority is to stop queue growth to avoid cascading failures. Do rollback first. If rollback fails due to pending pods, then enforce per-route throttling to protect core customers.

Sara K: rolling back now to lm-v3-stable. Command: `redwoodctl rollout set model=lm-v3-stable --target=prod --strategy=immediate`

infra-eng-bot: Received rollout command, creating reversal. Noting >800 pods in warmup state, commands may queue.

Alex W: also conditional plan to warm up smaller model variant and route heavy customers there. Megan, add acme-inc and searchly to priority bypass so they get routed to dedicated pool if available.

Megan R: done — added lists in the incident doc. Messaging: initial customer notification drafted, short blurb: "We are experiencing elevated errors/latency for generation endpoints while we mitigate a model rollout; engineer teams are on it and we will follow up with updates." Approving to send.

Jamie L: taking oncall now — assigning to myself for the next 2 hours. Steps I will run:
1) confirm rollback completion
2) check autoscaler quota with cloud acct (possible vendor throttle)
3) if rollback not successful, apply rate-limiter on /generate route and enable fallback to lm-v2-lite for non-critical traffic
4) coordinate capacity bump with infra if quota can be increased quickly

Jamie L: running `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep lm-v4-hotwarmup | wc -l` shows 420 pods still terminating/warmup. Progress slow.

Alex W: note — the model has a long KV cache warmup pattern due to a recent tokenizer change in v4 that increases context prefill. That is the root cause for per-pod memory churn. We need a postmortem on the tokenizer change impact on warmup cost.

Sara K: autoscaler cloud errors: `RequestLimitExceeded` then `QuotaExceeded`. I'll call vendor ops channel, maybe a temporary quota bump is possible.

infra-eng-bot: Cloud quota request submitted (req-8591). Estimated approval ETA 25-40m.

TJ (oncall): while we wait, applying soft rate limit to public endpoints to cap RPS per API key to 0.5x baseline and enable 503 backoff so clients will retry gracefully. Command: `rconsole route update /v1/generate --concurrency=50 --burst=100`

Alex W: putting an autoscale-safe fallback: update routing policy to prefer lm-v3-stable for known high-throughput keys. Patch: `redwoodctl route set policy=prefer:model=lm-v3-stable --selector=tag:high-traffic`

Megan R: Customer comms sent to affected customers with note about temporary degraded performance and mitigation steps. I'll escalate to account teams for acme-inc and searchly.

Jamie L: rollback completed for 85% traffic, but a subset of requests still hit lm-v4 due to sticky routing (edge caches). Purging edge cache for rollout id 20260315-16: `edgectl purge --id 20260315-16`

Alex W: after purge, queue dropped to ~300, p95 latency trending down to 1.1s. Good sign.

Sara K: autoscaler still reporting failures for additional replicas due to cloud quota. If quota stays limited, we need to keep rollout paused and verify model parameter changes (tokenizer/context) before re-trying.

Jamie L: immediate next actions:
- Keep rollout paused and mark lm-v4-hotwarmup as blocked in deploy dashboard.
- Open a high-priority ticket for research/ML to investigate tokenizer warmup behavior.
- Schedule a follow-up 30m synchronous to confirm stability and whether to request permanent quota bump.

Alex W: technical notes for postmortem:
- Root cause: model v4's tokenizer + KV prefill increased per-request warmup allocation, causing longer pod warmup and increased memory pressure.
- Contributing factor: autoscaler max_replicas config was conservative and cloud quota prevented transient ramp.
- Mitigations applied: immediate rollback, edge purge, per-route rate limiting, routing policy to fallback model, customer notifications, vendor quota request.

Megan R: impact summary for postmortem header:
- Duration: ~16:00 - 16:45 UTC (queue growth peaked 16:02)
- Affected: ~3 production customers, ~12k requests failed/429s (estimate)
- Business impact: degraded SLAs for paying customers, support escalations opened.

Jamie L: marking incident as active, severity S3 -> S2 (customer impact with partial mitigation). Assigning tasks:
- Alex W: produce logs & timeline (ETA 2h)
- Sara K: vendor quota follow-up, autoscaler logs (ETA 30m)
- Megan R: customer comms & account follow-ups (ongoing)
- ML team (cc @ml-research): investigate tokenizer change (urgent)

TJ (oncall): leaving a quick runbook note to avoid reintroducing lm-v4 until warmup cost is quantified and autoscaler max_replicas adjusted.

Alex W: adding experiment metric for future rollouts: warmup CPU/mem delta per model version during first 30m. Add as gating metric.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-07. Channel pinned and timeline started. Next update in 15m or on status change. :thumbsup:

Megan R: thanks team. I'll keep customers updated and collect any support logs. Please add any extra notes here and we'll capture them in the postmortem draft. :white_check_mark:"
